subject: mathematics
question_text: If a = 2i+j−3k, b = i−2j+k, c = −i+j−4k and d = i+j+k, then compute |(a×b)×(c×d)|.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.35 — LAQ chapter 4 Product of Vectors, answer 21.2, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). Printed appearances: TS 15. FOUR vectors, not three — the only question in the chapter with a d, and the structure is a cross product OF two cross products.⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer (its page is set two questions to a page in two columns, which takes the margin those tags would occupy). It follows the shape of the split the same chapter DOES print for answer 23 on book p.37, weighting each cross product against the closing step. The book's chapter header carries ★★★ and reads '7 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section C runs Q18-Q24 at 7 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q22 is the Product of Vectors slot. Re-cut to the 8-mark Section-C form of the 2026-27 pattern (TGBIE model paper w.e.f. 2026-27): the extra mark goes to Cross the two results.

recall_prompt: Say how you would compute this — say what you work out first when there are four vectors.

steps.label: Write what is given
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own. Copy the three (or four) vectors out once, in i, j, k order. Every cross product below is read straight off these rows, so a slip here is repeated three times.
steps.memory_tip: Copy all four vectors out once in i, j, k order. A slip here is repeated in three determinants.
lines: c = −i + j − 4k,  d = i + j + k

recall.must_convey: That the given vectors are written out before any product is computed. Naming the step is full credit.
accept: write the given vectors out first
copy down a b and c before starting
note the given vectors in i j k form
ichina vectors ni modata rasta
start by writing what is given

steps.why: A cross product is a determinant whose rows ARE these vectors. Laying them out once, aligned, is what makes each determinant readable.
common_mistakes: Missing a zero component and shifting a whole row.
Copying a sign wrongly and carrying it through every product.

steps.label: Find a×b
steps.margin_note: Two of the eight marks. Work the brackets first, exactly as in arithmetic. To check the result, dot it with a and with b — both must come to 0.
steps.memory_tip: Brackets first, exactly as in arithmetic. Check a cross product by dotting it with both original vectors — both must give 0.

recall.must_convey: That a×b is computed first and comes to −5i − 5j − 5k.
accept: work out a cross b first, it comes to minus five i minus five j minus five k
the first bracket gives all components minus five
expand the determinant for a cross b
a cross b anni components minus five vasthai
compute the inner bracket a cross b

steps.why: The outer operation cannot start until both brackets are single vectors. Brackets first is the same rule as in ordinary algebra.
common_mistakes: Trying to expand the whole expression at once.
Sign slip on the j term.

steps.label: Find c×d
steps.margin_note: Two more marks. The second bracket, built the same way from c and d.
steps.memory_tip: The second bracket, built the same way from c and d.

recall.must_convey: That c×d is computed as the second bracket, giving 5i − 3j − 2k.
accept: then c cross d gives five i minus three j minus two k
compute the second bracket c cross d
do the same for c and d
c cross d five i minus three j minus two k vasthundi
work out the other bracket

steps.why: Two independent brackets means two independent determinants — an error in one does not touch the other, which is worth knowing when checking.
common_mistakes: Computing d×c and reversing the signs.
Carrying a component of a or b into this determinant.

steps.label: Cross the two results
steps.margin_note: Three marks. Now cross the two results — a third determinant, with (1) on the first row and (2) on the second. Taking 5 out at the end makes the magnitude easy.
steps.memory_tip: A third determinant, with (1) on the first row and (2) on the second. Take the 5 out at the end.

recall.must_convey: That the two results are crossed in a third determinant, giving −5i − 35j + 40k, and that 5 is taken out as a common factor.
accept: cross the two results in another determinant to get minus five i minus thirty five j plus forty k, then take five out
take the cross product of the two brackets and factor out the five
a third determinant with the two results as rows
rendu results ni malli cross cheste, five common teeyyochu
cross the answers of the two brackets together

steps.why: Pulling the 5 out before taking the magnitude turns √(25 + 1225 + 1600) into 5√(1 + 49 + 64) — the same number, with much smaller arithmetic.
common_mistakes: Crossing in the wrong order, which flips the sign.
Squaring the large numbers instead of factoring first.

steps.label: Take the magnitude
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The 5 comes out of the square root as a multiplier. √114 does not simplify, so the surd stands.
steps.memory_tip: The 5 comes out of the root as a multiplier. √114 does not simplify, so the surd stands.

recall.must_convey: That the magnitude is 5√114, with the 5 carried outside the root.
accept: the magnitude is five root one hundred fourteen
five times root of one plus forty nine plus sixty four
it comes to five root one fourteen
five root one fourteen vasthundi
take the modulus to get five root one hundred and fourteen

steps.why: A factor outside a vector comes outside its magnitude as its absolute value — which is why the 5 multiplies the root rather than sitting inside it.
common_mistakes: Trying to simplify √114, which has no square factor.

insider_note: Four vectors and three cross products, taken in order: a×b first, then c×d, then cross those two. The common factor 5 comes out of the FINAL vector, which is what makes the magnitude easy.
